title: The boat and the monkey, twin masts, and two letters that land as n

slides.heading: Two letters that change their minds
body: Two consonants: a rolled r, and an l.
Put them last in a word and they turn into the same sound.
And a vowel that is last lesson's, written twice.

slides.heading: Pen and paper
body: Real paper, a real pen.
Both halves of the name, out loud.

slides.heading: The boat
body: Its name is the sound, then a word beginning with that sound.
The word means a **boat**.
A rolled r, like a motor turning over.

slides.heading: Rope, and the line above it
body: Every boat flies a pennant, and that is how you know whose is in.
The head sits low, at the waterline.
The line flies up and hooks over to the right.

slides.heading: The boat's letter
body: The head low, down at the waterline.
One line flying up, hooking right.

slides.heading: Write it
body: **Start at the head**, low, clockwise.
Up, and hook over to the right.
Roll it hard in careful speech, barely at all when talking fast.

slides.heading: The monkey
body: Its name is the sound, then a word beginning with that sound.
The word means a **monkey**.
A light l off the tongue ridge.

slides.heading: The one everybody swears at
body: It lives on the last post and steals whatever is uncovered.
Long, loose and leaping down the row.
The head at the base, and a tail arching over its back.

slides.heading: The monkey's letter
body: The head at the base.
One long tail, arching up and over.

slides.heading: Write it, and look at the two together
body: **Start at the head**, at the base, clockwise.
The tail arches up and over.
Put it beside the boat, and write both names underneath.

slides.heading: Last in a word, they are the same letter
body: At the **front** of a syllable: a rolled r, and an l.
Last in a syllable: **both** of them are n.
The mouse's letter, from lesson one.

slides.heading: And the set of five still stands
body: Lesson two: five hummable endings, and **that is still the whole set**.
These two stay outside the set.
They arrive **as** the mouse's letter, and are read as one.

slides.heading: Read this one
body: Chicken, long vowel, and the boat's letter at the end.
**Remember what it does there.** Out loud before you turn it over.

slides.heading: That one
body: **การ** — ends on **n**, with no roll at all.
It turns up inside longer words unchanged.

slides.prompt: A syllable is written with the boat's letter in last position. What sound ends it, and is the syllable live or dead?

answers: **Live** — because n is one of the hummable five.
It takes the live rule for its class, as the mouse's letter would.

slides.heading: The same mast, raised twice
body: Two masts, side by side, ahead of the consonant.
**Written first, spoken second** — exactly as last lesson.
The sound is the vowel in *cat*, held long.

slides.heading: Write it
body: Two uprights with a curve at the top of each.
Written **ahead of** the consonant.
Say each syllable aloud, with the consonant leading.

slides.heading: Read this one
body: Twin masts, the child's letter, the snake closing it.
**Watch the order.** Out loud before you turn it over.

slides.heading: That one
body: **แดง** — red.
Live ending, low class, and the tone comes out flat.

slides.heading: And the short one
body: **แ-ะ** — twin masts in front, the two hooks **ะ** behind.
The same shortener as lesson four and lesson seven.

slides.heading: And you have been reading it since lesson one
body: **และ** — twin masts, monkey's letter, two hooks.
That is the short vowel you just met.
It means *and*, and it is the 21st commonest word in Thai.

slides.heading: What happens when something follows it
body: Two hooks behind, a final consonant wants the spot, the hooks climb.
Same sound, same length. The mark moves up over the letter.
**No example today.** The common ones need a lesson-12 letter.

slides.prompt: You know one mast and two masts. Say which sound each carries, and what both of them do to reading order.

answers: Both written ahead of the consonant, both voiced after it.
Every mast after this one works the same way.

slides.heading: Seventeen letters
body: Seventeen letters, thirteen vowels.
Two new letters, and no new endings to remember.
Next: three market letters at once, and a leaning mast.
